messages:
maria (PM): Quick sync — we need to pick an approach for Dedicated capacity guarantees. Customers asking for guaranteed burst for predictable events (demos, launches). Thoughts?

sanjay (Eng): We can do two primitives: 1) hard reserved pools (capacity pinned) and 2) soft quotas with burst allowances backed by autoscale. Each has different SW and cost implications.

leah (Sales): Major enterprise customer asked for 6x normal peak for 2 hours monthly. They want hard guarantee; procurement will ask for SLA.

ashley (CS): Also saw smaller customers wanting on-demand burst but without enterprise pricing. Prefer a cheaper soft-burst model.

tony (Infra): Hard reserved pools = idle dedicated hardware or pre-warmed nodes. Predictable but expensive. Soft quotas can be served with burst tokens + preemption rules.

maria (PM): So prioritization question: do we build MVP soft-burst (cheaper, faster to ship) vs invest months in reserved pools UI + billing + SLA? Launch criteria will differ.

sanjay (Eng): Minimal viable soft-burst design: per-customer quota + ephemeral burst up to X% of reserved, with automatic fallback to lower-tier model when exhausted. Implementation ~6 weeks if we reuse current autoscaler hooks.

maria (PM): Proposed launch criteria for soft-burst: 1) config UI to set soft quota & burst window, 2) metric-level RBAC, 3) clear telemetry + dashboard, 4) fallback behavior defined and tested.

leah (Sales): For enterprise deals we need hard reserved pools in roadmap, but we can close smaller ones on soft-burst. Need comms: "not SLA-backed" disclaimers.

ashley (CS): Add acceptance criteria: simulate 3x traffic for 30m w/ no errors and <2x latency degradation. Also alerting when soft-burst drains.

sanjay (Eng): Rough config snippet for soft-burst (for discussion):
```
soft_quota:
  base_qps: 100
  burst_tokens: 300
  burst_window_secs: 600
  fallback: "reduced_model"  # fallback path when tokens exhausted
autoscale:
  ramp_up_secs: 120
  cooldown_secs: 300
```

tony (Infra): That looks fine. Need to decide token refill logic: time-window vs leaky-bucket. Leaky-bucket preferred to avoid sync spikes.

maria (PM): Pricing: we could bill soft-burst consumption at premium rate but not require commitment. Leah, can you run a quick price-sensitivity check?

leah (Sales): Yep. I'll check similar offers and report back by EOD. Small ask: can we show an estimate cost in Console during config? That helps sales.

maria (PM): For hard reserved pools we need separate acceptance: provisioning flow, cancellation, billing commit, SLA page, runbook for failover. That's a Q3 epic.

sanjay (Eng): One more nuance: multi-tenant vs single-tenant reserved pools. Single-tenant simpler for isolation & compliance. Multi-tenant reserved pools needs isolation controls in the scheduler. Higher SRE effort.

ashley (CS): Compliance customers lean single-tenant. Important to call out in roadmap doc.

maria (PM): Decision proposal: ship soft-burst MVP first (priority P0), expose config and dashboards, ship billing + UI + alerts. Parallel discovery for reserved pools (P1) with design spike to estimate effort. Agree?

leah (Sales): +1 from GTM. Helps land mid-market deals quickly.

sanjay (Eng): +1 engineering. We'll schedule a 2-week spike for reserved pool requirements and list dependencies.

tony (Infra): I'll scope infra costs for both options and share a cost model.

ops-bot: Created task PROD-4821: "Soft-burst MVP: quota, burst tokens, fallback path" assigned to eng-team.

maria (PM): OK — I'll convert this into a short PRD and include launch criteria. Assigning owners: Sanjay for implementation, Tony for infra cost model, Leah for pricing feedback, Ashley for acceptance tests. Back to this thread for any blockers. :white_check_mark:
